elements.element: The liability cap must apply mutually to both parties on equivalent scope and terms.
elements.evidence: Both parties have a cap, but the scopes are asymmetric: Contractor's cap covers only liability relating to performance of Services under a Statement of Work, while Company's cap covers liability arising out of the entire Agreement.

elements.element: The fee-based cap limb must use a 12-month period preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Both cap sentences use fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim.

elements.element: The fee-based cap limb must include fees paid.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly includes fees paid to Contractor.

elements.element: The fee-based cap limb must include fees payable.
elements.evidence: The clause refers only to fees paid and does not include accrued or otherwise payable fees.

elements.element: The cap must include USD 1,000,000 as the alternative benchmark.
elements.evidence: No USD 1,000,000 benchmark appears.

elements.element: The cap must equal the greater of the 12-month fee limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no greater-of formulation or monetary floor.

elements.element: Indirect damages must be excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (b) states that neither party is liable to the other for indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages must be excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (b) states that neither party is liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, and Excluded Claims are expressly uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Data protection obligations are not included in Excluded Claims. The unidentified Paragraph 9 exception cannot be credited as satisfying this requirement.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Security obligations are not included in Excluded Claims. The unidentified Paragraph 9 exception cannot be credited as satisfying this requirement.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's indemnification obligations and are uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's gross negligence and are uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include willful misconduct and are uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for fraud must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Fraud is not included in Excluded Claims or otherwise expressly carved out.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: Direct intellectual-property infringement claims are not expressly carved out; the indemnification carve-out does not necessarily cover such claims.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations must be stated not to constitute damages for purposes of the cap.
elements.evidence: No payment-obligation exclusion appears, and Company's maximum-liability provision broadly applies for any reason arising out of the Agreement.

elements.element: The liability cap must apply mutually to both parties on equivalent scope and terms.
elements.evidence: Contractor's cap remains limited to liability relating to performance of Services under a Statement of Work, whereas Company's cap extends to liability arising out of the entire Agreement.

elements.element: Each party's cap must be measured by 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: Each cap is calculated using fees paid to Contractor in the twelve months preceding the claim.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims, expressly uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim, expressly uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's gross negligence is an Excluded Claim, expressly uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct must be uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's willful misconduct is an Excluded Claim, expressly uncapped for either party.

result.reason: The redline adds the fallback fee lookback and all four required fallback carve-outs, but it does not create a genuinely mutual cap because Contractor's cap remains materially narrower in scope than Company's. The preferred position also lacks payable fees, the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, several required carve-outs, and the payment-obligation clarification. The changes are confined to liability-cap mechanics and do not disturb unrelated terms, although the placement of the global Excluded Claims exception is somewhat awkward.
